search_strategy: Cloned the repo and read cost.py/status trackers/request_processor code exhaustively first (steps 1-20), correctly flagging the four separate cost() implementations and the ad-hoc external/litellm split named in the ticket. For chat, ran a mix of full per-day channel dumps (grep-style listing of a channel's messages by date) and Mattermost's /api/v4/.../posts/search keyword endpoint for specific terms ('unknown_provider','unknown_model','UnpricedModelError','ModelPrice','batch_multiplier','batch rate','inferred','asterisk'); the keyword search sometimes returned only a one-line snippet per hit rather than the full thread (this is exactly what caused the l11 partial-find and probably others). For wiki, it never called /api/search at all — instead it built its own page-dump script (bs.py) that fetches /api/pages/{id} (body+comments) for a hand-picked shortlist of page ids (140, 142, 132, 139, 164, 209) inferred from context/handover mentions in chat/mail rather than from a systematic title or full-text search; this missed at least 4 of the 7 comment-bearing pages (ws-050, releases/v0-1-22, weekly-notes-apr-14, and whichever page fix18/s3-l1 would have needed) entirely, including the one page (ws-050) that states the lost observability fact outright. For mail, it used IMAP SEARCH TEXT for specific terms ('inferred','asterisk','batch_multiplier','cost processor','WS-054','PR 681' etc.) and fetched whole threads once a candidate was found; this worked well for the threads it thought to search for, but never tried 'inference.net', 'PR 565' as a raw phrase, or '#cookbooks'-adjacent terms, leaving those threads/channels completely unvisited. No truncation-by-head or crashed helper meaningfully lost content that mattered to the graded facts, except that the wiki dump script crashed once on a malformed comments-parsing assumption (page 140) and was promptly fixed and re-run successfully.
end_reason: Run completed normally: commit merged to main, CI green, service redeployed and healthy (provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1). reward=0.8571 reflects exactly one lost fact (g6.r1.observability) out of seven, not a systemic failure.
notable: Line 7136/msg185: the agent implemented non-raising 'degrade' behaviour only inside BatchStatusTracker/OnlineStatusTracker.refresh_model_price(), which is what the TICKET itself explicitly asks for (item 8, 'Never raises'). It never extended the same pattern to the four cost-processor cost() methods, because the hidden requirement that demands that generalisation (g6.r1.l12) was never read.

Lines 1687/1701-1843: the agent explicitly recognised and correctly dismissed a decoy wiki page (140, describing an alternate never-raising `lookup_price`/`ModelPrice.input_per_1k` contract) while still extracting the genuine planted clue (g6.r1.l8) from its comment thread — good source discrimination.

VERSION DRIFT (lines 2252-2271, 2305-2323): the mail thread carrying g6.r2.g6r2-s2-l4 in the actual v6 world this run played against reads with the OPPOSITE polarity from the repo's v7 answer key. This run's world has emil say 'the half-of-table figure it returned is the bug, not the answer... Put the table figure on the sheet, not the halved one; I will raise it... the halving on that line is the thing to fix.' The v7 key quotes the same thread as 'the half-of-table figure it returned is the correct answer... put the halved number on the sheet.' The two are inversions of each other on whether klusterai batch pricing should be halved. Luckily for this run, the v6 wording argues FOR the correct final rule (klusterai never discounted), so it did not mislead the agent, but graders comparing this transcript against the v7 key text verbatim would misjudge this remark.

Neither of the two herrings (the January 27 'settled' x2-cancellation belief) was ever read directly — the agent only encountered them secondhand, restated inside the two reversal threads themselves (lines 3253, 2997), while those threads were being read specifically to confirm the CURRENT design. This means the agent was never actually at risk of following the herring; it only ever saw the belief framed as already-overturned history.

The agent's own test suite (test_cost.py) tests batch_multiplier() and resolve_model_price() raising/degrading in isolation, but never tests that an _ExternalTableCostProcessor's cost() method itself survives an unpriced model — a gap that exactly predicts the graded failure and shows the agent never registered 'every cost() method degrades' as a requirement to verify, only as a tracker-level one.
